clue.text: Call girls knocked back, say, by youth leader's plan

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word for the call girls is read in reverse

parts.note: call girls are prostitutes, in slang tarts
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, taken here from youth

explanation.surface: A seedy scheme: a youth leader arranges call girls, who are then turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall scheme or course of action, a synonym of plan.

clue.text: A woman in bed is unable to

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the word for the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman lying in bed apparently can't do something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is unable to is a direct paraphrase of the negative modal verb meaning lacking ability.

clue.text: Barker's surprised cry when catching a nail

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the cry surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: lor! is a dated exclamation of surprise, from Lord!
a brad is a thin wire nail with a small head

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in surprise on snagging themselves on a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of dog, and a dog is something that barks: a crossword-style definition by action.

clue.text: Sort of wedding disheartened old Japanese commander

indicators.note: disheartened means having lost its heart, so the central letter of the wedding word goes

parts.note: a shotgun wedding is one forced on the couple, typically because of a pregnancy

explanation.surface: A grim forced wedding left an old Japanese military leader downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan before 1868, so an old Japanese commander.

clue.text: Alleged lover securing introduction to roving reporter

indicators.note: securing means holding fast within, so the lover word encloses the letter

parts.note: in a divorce case the co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the spouse

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter, here of roving

explanation.surface: A person cited in a divorce takes on a roving journalist's introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The co-respondent is a British divorce-court term: the third party alleged to have committed adultery with the respondent.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a particular subject.

clue.text: Delayed, little boy finally runs to centre

indicators.note: to centre sends the runs letter into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: a tad means a little bit
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of boy

explanation.surface: A small boy is late, having finally run to the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little boy' looks like one unit, but 'little' gives TAD and 'boy finally' gives Y; R goes into the middle of TADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardy means late or slow to arrive, a near synonym of delayed.

clue.text: Meat brought in before noon: last of chicken leg for king

indicators.note: brought in puts the meat word inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: a.m. means before noon
game is the meat of wild animals or birds hunted for food

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of chicken

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A menu note: meat comes before noon, then a chicken leg for the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side and the on side are the same half of a cricket field, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Daughter, thought to have lost head, turned aside

indicators.note: to have lost head means the first letter of the word for thought is removed

parts.note: reflected means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: A daughter, believed to have panicked, swerved away.
explanation.definitionFit: Deflected means diverted from a course, so turned aside describes it exactly.

clue.text: Agitate Arab leader on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means as heard spoken over the airwaves, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab chief, often pronounced to rhyme with bake

explanation.surface: Is an Arab ruler broadcasting to stir people up?
explanation.definitionFit: To shake something is to agitate it, moving it rapidly to and fro.

clue.text: They engage people who arrive outside embassy

indicators.note: outside means the arrivals word wraps round the embassy word

parts.note: comers are people who come or arrive
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Diplomats hire new arrivals waiting outside the embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission someone is to engage them for a task, so those who commission work are ones who engage.

clue.text: Old-maidish teacher recalled in spy novel

indicators.note: in places the reversed teacher inside the rearranged spy letters
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of spy are rearranged
recalled means called back, so the teacher word is read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A fussy schoolteacher features in a spy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy novel' reads as a book genre, but 'novel' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prissy means primly fussy and prudish, the manner stereotypically attributed to an old maid.

clue.text: State of Newcastle supporter introducing 1960s pop?

indicators.note: introducing means the music follows on after the supporter

parts.note: NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne
a bra is a supporting undergarment
ska is Jamaican popular music of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A Newcastle United fan brings 1960s pop music into the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle is a city in north-east England; NE is its postcode prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Depressed fellow associated with tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
Ken is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: A man is gloomy because of his link with a gutter newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in reverse order to the clue: the Sun, a British tabloid, then KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken means lying below the surrounding level, so depressed in the physical sense.

clue.text: Condition that retro pub stops supplying mineral

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the reversed pub goes inside the condition word

parts.note: state means condition, as in a state of repair

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the pub word is reversed

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Some situation is stopping an old-fashioned pub from supplying a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannite is a tin-bearing sulphide ore, one of the minerals.

clue.text: Around Jersey, etc, loneliness engenders concern

indicators.note: around means the loneliness word surrounds the islands abbreviation

parts.note: solitude is the state of being alone
Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

explanation.surface: Isolation on Jersey and its neighbours makes people worried.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands, including Jersey and Guernsey, lie off the coast of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care for someone's welfare, that is, concern.

clue.text: Cut of meat — something served up when duke is absent

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
D, the abbreviation for duke, is absent, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: in badminton the shuttlecock, served to start each rally, is called a bird

explanation.surface: A dinner served without the duke present: rib of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' suggests a dish, but it is a badminton bird (shuttlecock); without D it is BIR, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib is a cut of meat including a rib bone, such as rib of beef.

clue.text: Woman keeping the Queen's decorative artwork

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the woman's name contains the letter

parts.note: Tracey is a woman's name
R, for Regina, is the Queen's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A woman holds on to the Queen's ornamental art.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental stone openwork in Gothic windows, a kind of decorative art.

clue.text: Officer involved in a pact with leaders of great publishing firm?

parts.note: a large publishing company is often a group of imprints

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters of in a pact are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military officer is mixed up in a deal with the heads of a big publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' is a cryptic nudge: the captains, or leaders, of a publishing group would be group captains.
explanation.definitionFit: A group captain is a senior Royal Air Force officer, ranking above wing commander.

clue.text: Sportsperson's obstruction revealed in a couple of articles

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, a link joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: revealed in means found inside, so the hindrance sits within the articles

parts.note: two articles, the indefinite a and the definite the
let means hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A sportsman's hurdle is exposed in a couple of newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Let means an obstruction, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance; it goes inside THE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sports, especially track and field.

clue.text: Near sensation of prickling restricting a singer

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the prickling word encloses the letter

parts.note: a tingle is a prickling or stinging feeling

explanation.surface: A singer stands close, feeling a prickle of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famed for its rich nocturnal song, so a singer.

clue.text: Very small fruit in yellow boxes

indicators.note: boxes means contains, so the phrase fruit in yellow holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A miniature fruit sits in yellow packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a straightforward synonym for minute, extremely little.

clue.text: Furious, caught in cool mountain range with little money!

indicators.note: in places the caught letter inside the cool and mountain words

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
the Andes is the South American mountain range
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged at being stranded in the cold Andes with little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' tempts as cold, but it is IN, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent, literally glowing with heat, is used figuratively for blazing with anger.

clue.text: Uncommon procedure involving female getting thinner

indicators.note: involving means bringing in alongside, so the female letter joins the procedure word at its front

parts.note: rare means uncommon
an action is a procedure, as a legal proceeding

explanation.surface: An unusual operation on a woman to help her lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' here just attaches F to the front of ACTION rather than putting it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefaction is the process of a gas or substance becoming less dense, i.e. thinning out.

clue.text: Attire sent flying in US motorway

indicators.note: sent flying means scattered, so the letters of attire sent are jumbled

explanation.surface: Clothing gets scattered across an American highway.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a highway in the US federal network linking states, the American equivalent of a motorway.

clue.text: Points about new graduates collectively

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the points enclose the other letters

parts.note: E and SE are two compass points
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates

explanation.surface: Fresh graduates get their marks counted as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase en masse means all together as a group, i.e. collectively.

clue.text: Singular pair managed to pinch old pouch

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: to pinch means to grab, so the pair and managed words hold the letter

parts.note: ran means managed, as of a business

explanation.surface: A strange couple contrived to steal an antique purse.
explanation.walkthrough: The pouch is the one worn in front of a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the leather pouch hung at the front of a kilt.

clue.text: Work over, turned up with son

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word up is read the other way

explanation.surface: A job is finished, and the son appeared to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived, but 'turned' reverses the word 'up' to give PU, between O and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is an artistic work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Heads of such knockabout institutions go downhill fast

indicators.note: heads of picks the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: Principals of rough-and-tumble schools are rapidly in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go downhill' suggests decline, but here it is literal: slide down a snowy slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide over snow on runners, often speeding down mountain slopes.
